shared_elements: standing/frontal human figure carved on an upright monolithic slab
figure occupying the full height of the surface
large head with prominent headdress or headgear at top
low-relief circular disc/rosette ornaments on the chest or torso
broad band across the lower body (belt/loincloth or apron)
schematic, low-relief carving of body ornament rather than modelled anatomy
legs/feet rendered small at the base
justification: Both depict a single frontal standing personage carved in low relief over the whole face of a tall upright slab, with a large elaborated head at the top, disc-like ornaments on the chest, and a broad band across the hips above stubby legs — a fairly specific shared scheme of a figure defined by ornament rather than modelled anatomy. The main differences are that A shows a densely detailed costume with hanging plumes, elaborate panels and much finer surface incision, while B is far more reduced and blocky, with a jutting beak-like head and only a few isolated motifs on an otherwise plain torso.
